exact_causal_gap: Cocoa256 is not a retained POSIX errno. The raw error has only present/domain/code and omits NSUnderlyingErrorKey. It does not identify the failing operation, prove successful writable open, prove any F_SET invocation, or identify Foundation's actual numeric class argument.

Capability-negative fstatfs observations surrounding the public operation do not prove which capability query or branch occurred inside Foundation. The result could reflect a different SET error, another failure, or a different installed implementation. Selecting one explanation now would be an unsupported assumption.

An underlying NSError chain plus a separate direct fcntl control can narrow the alternatives, but matching errors are not a trace of the public setter's own call. Exact suppression attribution requires runtime-bound evidence linking that invocation to its primitive arguments/outcomes and handling branch. Attribution to A37 additionally requires the corresponding failed Simulator/app path, not only a fresh host-file experiment.

interpretation_rules: An actual underlying POSIX errno narrows the public error but alone does not identify open versus SET. A separate raw SET failure records that control's actual failure, not proof Foundation made the identical call.

Public FALSE plus ENOTSUP/clear-capability evidence must not be described as observed public-success suppression. If compared with the retained tag, the discrepancy is evidence that its applicability still needs establishment, not permission to rewrite the observation.

A same-class SET success proves only acceptance of that argument on that descriptor. A missing public Complete class constant is not a simulated SET result. Even an SDK-qualified Complete SET success requires actual post-read class evidence and still would not establish enforcement.
